note.title: Othello — plot, tragedy and Iago’s characterisation
note.overview: Secure the plot needed for analysis and focus on how Shakespeare constructs Iago through language, dramatic form and manipulation.
learningGoals: Explain Iago’s role in the tragedy.
Identify dramatic methods used in characterisation.
Analyse manipulation rather than relying on labels.
mustMemoriseRules: Plot knowledge supports analysis; it is not the analysis itself.
Separate what Iago says publicly from what the audience learns privately.
A method should be linked to its effect on another character and/or the audience.
workedExamples: Dramatic irony can expose the gap between Iago’s public persona and the audience’s knowledge of his plotting.
The handkerchief becomes persuasive not because it proves guilt, but because Iago controls how Othello interprets it.
commonMistakes: Retelling the plot instead of analysing method.
Calling Iago evil without explaining construction.
Treating a character’s belief as an objective fact.
detailedExplanation: The curriculum scope and assessed skills are verified against the official Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 English Curriculum Outline 2026-27.
Plot and method questions support the school focus on Othello and Iago; longer paragraph tasks are app practice, not the teacher’s live timed assessment.
Long open responses do not by themselves create formal Mastery evidence.
examTips: Use plot knowledge only when it supports an interpretation.
Distinguish what characters believe from what the audience knows.
Analyse Shakespeare’s method rather than attaching labels.
Keep a coherent line of argument.
quickCheck: Explain Iago’s role in the tragedy.
Identify dramatic methods used in characterisation.
Analyse manipulation rather than relying on labels.
beforeStartingPractice: Recall the character relationships and central deception before practice.
